title: Fiscal Policy and Government Spending
text: Fiscal policy refers to government decisions about taxation and spending to influence the economy. Expansionary fiscal policy — increasing government spending or cutting taxes — stimulates economic activity and is typically used during recessions. Contractionary fiscal policy — cutting spending or raising taxes — cools inflationary pressure. The fiscal multiplier measures how much GDP changes relative to a change in government spending. High levels of government debt can crowd out private investment by raising interest rates. The debate between fiscal austerity and stimulus is a perennial issue in economic policy, with Keynesian economists generally favoring stimulus and classical/supply-side economists favoring deficit reduction.
